statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-32316 (GHSA-q3h9-m34w-h76f, https://github.com/jqlang/jq/security/advisories/GHSA-q3h9-m34w-h76f): through jq 1.8.1, jvp_string_append() and jvp_string_copy_replace_bad() compute the buffer size in a 32-bit unsigned integer, so concatenating strings longer than 2^31 bytes in total allocates a far too small heap buffer and the copy overflows it. It is fixed by https://github.com/jqlang/jq/commit/e47e56d226519635768e6aab2f38f0ab037c09e5, first released in jq 1.8.2 (https://github.com/jqlang/jq/releases/tag/jq-1.8.2). Checked every jq package in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository for x86_64 and aarch64: 1.8.1-r0 is upstream jq 1.8.1 with Alpine's 3.23 patches, 1.8.1_git20260429-r1 is the same plus upstream commit e47e56d (the CVE-2026-32316 fix), and 1.8.2_git20260622-r1 and 1.8.2_git20261021-r2 are upstream jq 1.8.2, as the version string in /usr/bin/jq and libjq confirms. 1.8.1-r0 lacks the fix; 1.8.1_git20260429-r1 and every later build carry it. The 'String too long' check the fix adds is present in libjq of every build on the fixed side and absent from every build on the affected side.

Checked every jq package in the DHI Alpine 3.24 repository for x86_64 and aarch64: 1.8.1_git20260609-r1 is upstream jq 1.8.1 plus upstream commit e47e56d (the CVE-2026-32316 fix), and 1.8.2_git20260622-r1 and 1.8.2_git20261021-r2 are upstream jq 1.8.2, as the version string in /usr/bin/jq and libjq confirms. CVE-2026-32316 (GHSA-q3h9-m34w-h76f, https://github.com/jqlang/jq/security/advisories/GHSA-q3h9-m34w-h76f): through jq 1.8.1, jvp_string_append() and jvp_string_copy_replace_bad() compute the buffer size in a 32-bit unsigned integer, so concatenating strings longer than 2^31 bytes in total allocates a far too small heap buffer and the copy overflows it. It is fixed by https://github.com/jqlang/jq/commit/e47e56d226519635768e6aab2f38f0ab037c09e5, first released in jq 1.8.2 (https://github.com/jqlang/jq/releases/tag/jq-1.8.2). Checked every jq build in the DHI Debian 13 repository for amd64 and arm64, using the changelog each package ships and its libjq: rebuilds of Debian 1.7.1-6+deb13u1 and 1.7.1-6+deb13u2, a 1.8.1-5 build (arm64 only) whose changelog is an unreleased Debian 1.8.1-5 snapshot from January 2026 with no 2026 security fixes, and a rebuild of Debian 1.8.2-1, which is upstream jq 1.8.2. Debian's 1.7.1-6+deb13u2 changelog lists this CVE, but the patch was missing: 1.7.1-6+deb13u3 (DSA-6416-1) adds it as 'missing patch for CVE-2026-32316', and Debian records trixie as fixed only in 1.7.1-6+deb13u3 (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-32316), which has no DHI rebuild. The 1.8.1-5 build predates the fix. Every build before the rebuild of 1.8.2-1 is therefore affected. The 'String too long' check the fix adds is present in libjq of every build on the fixed side and absent from every build on the affected side.
